title: Growing Trees
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Each learner plants and cares for a tree in the school compound or at home, from a seedling, seed or cutting, with a name tag and a care record.

skills.key_step: The child explains why trees matter: they hold soil, break wind, give shade and oxygen, take in carbon dioxide, hold rain in forests that feed rivers, give homes to wildlife, and give fruit, timber, fodder, medicine and fuel.

floor.question: Which gas do we breathe in to live?

representations: a map of Kenya's water towers
pictures of a bare and a forested hillside
steps: Air: oxygen in, carbon dioxide out.

board.do: Draw a hill with trees and a hill without.
Ask which hill keeps its soil after heavy rain.

misconceptions.ask: What do trees do to the land?
misconceptions.repair: Compare the soil under a tree's shade with bare ground at midday; talk about cover, humus and springs in forests.

misconceptions.ask: Which gas do trees give out?
misconceptions.repair: Recall air components from Science: plants take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen in daylight.
List what a mango or grevillea gives over its life: fruit, shade, timber, fodder, bees, windbreak.

listen_for: They do not; rivers come from the sea
misconceptions.ask: How do forests help rivers like the Tana?
misconceptions.repair: Show the Mau or Mount Kenya forests on a map and the rivers flowing out of them.

checks.question: Give two ways trees help the environment.
checks.answer: any two of holding soil, shade, oxygen, rain and rivers, wildlife homes

checks.question: Which gas do trees take in?

skills.key_step: The child says how a tree is planted and cared for: choose a suitable tree and site, dig early, topsoil apart and mixed with manure, remove the sleeve, plant at the nursery depth, firm, water, mulch, fence, then water and weed until established.

floor.prerequisite: Knows how a fruit seedling is planted.
floor.question: What is mixed with topsoil when planting?

steps: Dig early; topsoil apart; add manure.
Remove the sleeve; plant at the same depth.

board.do: Draw a seedling in a polythene sleeve going into a hole.
Ask what to do with the sleeve.
Write "remove the sleeve, keep the soil ball".

listen_for: Leave it on to protect the roots
misconceptions.ask: What is done with the seedling's polythene sleeve when planting?
misconceptions.repair: Show roots curled inside a sleeve dug up after a year.

listen_for: Right next to the house wall
misconceptions.ask: Where should a tree that grows big be planted?
misconceptions.repair: Show a tree whose roots have cracked a wall.

listen_for: Only on the day it is planted
misconceptions.ask: How long must a newly planted tree be cared for?
misconceptions.repair: Show a care record and seedlings that died after planting day.

listen_for: It does not matter which tree
misconceptions.ask: Why is eucalyptus not planted beside springs and wetlands?
misconceptions.repair: Ask the class which indigenous trees grow by rivers in their area.

checks.question: Why is the topsoil kept apart when digging?
checks.answer: it is the richest soil, to go back round the roots

checks.question: Why fence a young tree?
checks.answer: to keep animals from eating or trampling it
